primary.body:
## Problem

GeoLibre works when opened directly and inside the HyperPBI Playground, but Power BI Desktop can leave the embedded component stuck at `Waiting for the pinned GeoLibre runtime handshake.`

Power BI can host custom visuals inside a sandboxed browsing context whose nested frames use an opaque serialized origin (`MessageEvent.origin === "null"`). HyperPBI previously required every GeoLibre message to have the normal HTTPS origin, so it discarded the real `geolibre:ready` message even when it came from the exact GeoLibre iframe window.

## Fix

- support two pinned message transports: normal HTTPS origin and opaque sandbox origin
- accept the opaque transport only from the exact GeoLibre iframe `contentWindow`
- pin the transport only after the expected GeoLibre version successfully completes the handshake
- prevent later messages from switching between strict and opaque origin modes
- use `postMessage(..., "*")` only after the opaque transport has been positively established; normal browser/runtime traffic remains exact-origin
- preserve project load/state and baseline selection events in the Power BI sandbox
- handle versioned `selectionChanged` events directly so GeoLibre -> Power BI interaction remains available without the public embed client
- add a managed-runtime fallback for `highlightFeature`, preserving Power BI/HyperPBI -> GeoLibre external highlighting when the public `@geolibre/embed` client cannot address an opaque child
- keep the public enhanced client for normal browser origins and keep it optional
- bump the PBIVIZ version to `1.0.1.3` so Power BI Desktop does not reuse the previous cached visual package

## Security/stability

The change does **not** globally trust null origins. HyperPBI still requires the message to come from the exact iframe WindowProxy, validates the pinned GeoLibre version before opening the opaque transport, then locks that transport for the lifetime of the adapter. Unexpected HTTPS origins and origin-mode changes are rejected.

## Regression coverage

- normal HTTPS-origin behavior still rejects attacker/null-origin traffic
- Power BI-style opaque handshake loads the project and uses `*` only after validation
- project state and selection events round-trip over the opaque transport
- external feature highlights use the managed opaque embed-command fallback
- invalid null-origin versions cannot pin the transport
- existing enhanced API, slow-start, timeout, and terminal-runtime behavior remain covered

## Validation

GitHub Actions CI is green on head `aac96563`:

- `npm ci`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run web:typecheck`
- `npm run web:build`
- `npm run web:sites:build`
- `npm test`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run docs:check`
- `npm run package:core`
- `npm run package:maps`
- `npm run package:verify`

The Vercel preview is also green. Final acceptance still requires importing the newly versioned Maps PBIVIZ into Power BI Desktop because CI cannot reproduce Microsoft's Desktop custom-visual host exactly.

No GeoLibre version upgrade is included. The managed runtime remains pinned to GeoLibre 2.5.0; this PR only fixes the Power BI Desktop transport boundary.
